claims.text: The identity of X (Si, Mn, or Al) governs whether CrFeCoNiX forms a stable, coherent protective oxide above 900 °C.
X controls scale stability by controlling the type and coherency of oxide nucleated at the metal/oxide interface.
Al or Si preferentially segregates near the alloy surface during high-temperature exposure.
Al or Si promotes formation of Al2O3 or SiO2 at the surface.
The Al2O3 or SiO2 layer is slow-growing, coherent, and adherent.
Al2O3 or SiO2 has low lattice mismatch with the underlying high-entropy-alloy matrix.
Mn-containing alloys form Mn oxides that tend to be non-coherent and volatile.
Non-coherent or volatile Mn-oxide scales are prone to cracking and spallation.
A crystallographically coherent Al2O3 or SiO2 interfacial layer provides a low-strain interface that resists spallation.
A dense, coherent Al- or Si-rich oxide lowers scale growth by reducing oxygen diffusion.
Good lattice matching of the oxide and substrate reduces thermal stresses.
Mn oxides have higher defect content and poorer lattice compatibility than the proposed Al- or Si-rich protective oxides.
The defect content and poor lattice compatibility of Mn oxides produce stress concentrations, microcracking, and eventual spallation.
CrFeCoNiAl and CrFeCoNiSi will develop thinner, continuous, adherent oxide scales during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
CrFeCoNiMn will develop thicker, cracked, and spalled oxide scales with inferior oxidation or corrosion resistance.
CrFeCoNi alloys lacking sufficient reactive-element content, or containing predominantly Mn, typically form unstable, spalled scales under the stated conditions.
The proposed behavior applies to equiatomic or near-equiatomic CrFeCoNiX alloys in single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution states above 900 °C.
Comparable pre-oxidation microstructures are required for the proposed X-dependent comparison.

contradictions.description: The intervention and boundary require temperatures above 900 °C, whereas the illustrative range is stated as 900–1100 °C and therefore includes 900 °C, which is not above 900 °C.
